title: Retry loop resets profile with shutil.rmtree(ignore_errors=True); on Windows a partial delete leaves Default/ without the ledger, so every later attempt dies at once with "Legacy occupied or unproved profile refused" and the retry cannot recover
repro: Wrong-action case, py -m pytest test_sb_join_ownership.py -k "native_same_host and wrong-action" on a loaded box: 5/5 FAIL (87s,64s,40s,72s,494s); the 494 s run ended with main.out = managed-driver + fatal RuntimeError(Legacy occupied or unproved profile refused) and a profile holding Default/ and first_party_sets.db but no .lkb-ownership.json
fix_direction: Verify the profile is gone after rmtree (retry delete, or use a fresh profile directory per attempt and pass that path), and surface the real attempt-1 failure instead of the retry artifact

title: Owner-liveness check runs before Job termination: a recycled owner PID makes --cleanup-only refuse ('Reused owner PID refused') and never reaches TerminateJobObject, so a Chrome that outlived its owner stays unreaped by cleanup
repro: Seen once in maker's 8-run verification (1 of 8 under heavy CPU load): test assertions passed, recorded Chrome outlived the exited owner for >190 s, 12x 'Cannot inspect owned Job', then 'Reused owner PID refused' (owner PID recycled by an unrelated process). NOT reproduced by checker: 8/8 wrong-action + full file 52/52 on a lighter box.
mechanism: sb_join_ownership.py ~L192-198: cleanup does identity(record.owner.pid); if a live process has that PID with a different create_time/exe it raises 'Reused owner PID refused' before the Job section. The owner is itself assigned to the kill-on-close Job (AssignProcessToJobObject(GetCurrentProcess)), so Chrome normally dies when the owner exits (measured 13-18 s idle). If that teardown is slow or does not fire under load, and Windows recycles the PID (fast under process churn), the only recovery path is closed: the named Job is identified by its nonce and membership of the recorded browser is verified, so Job termination does not depend on the owner PID. Safe-by-design refusal, but it converts a delayed reap into a permanent leak until the profile is cleaned by hand. Why Chrome outlived the owner >190 s is unexplained (unreproduced).
fix_direction: Treat a mismatched live process at the owner PID as 'owner gone' (owner = None) and continue to the Job path, which already proves containment by named Job + IsProcessInJob; keep refusing only when the owner identity matches (still alive). Add a deterministic test with a stubbed identity() returning a different created time. Separately investigate why kill-on-close lagged >190 s.
severity_note: medium: needs kill-on-close lag AND PID reuse; leaks a headless bot Chrome per occurrence in live use; test-only cycle is not affected
